snapshots.label: Sunday daily

projection.scoring_basis: DraftKings NFL Classic; estimates attributed to provider, not Codex point forecasts

picks.rationale: Keep the Stafford–Nacua pairing at its verified price; Arizona remains a favorable matchup, while a lopsided Rams win could reduce passing volume.
Keep the Rams backfield anchor. He provides a rushing path alongside the Stafford–Nacua passing pairing; three Rams still concentrate the lineup.
Hall remains ruled out. Keep the replacement lead-back opportunity at $5,700, while treating the road matchup and receiving workload as risks.
Keep the premium Rams receiver rather than weaken the core to spend the last $300. His sourced model estimate remains the highest among the listed receivers.
Keep the Giants receiving anchor. Team reporting confirms that Nabers and Likely both supported substantial production last week; the two selections now share offensive risk.
Keep the $4,000 WR slot with Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek ruled out. Extra opportunity is plausible; a high-volume receiving role is still an assumption.
Keep the $4,100 tight end. The consistent external model still prefers him to the $3,900 Goedert alternative, and switching would not independently fund a core upgrade.
Replace Allgeier with Likely at the same price. Recent target volume and Theo Johnson's confirmed absence support receiving opportunity; do not assume last week's touchdowns repeat.
Keep Pittsburgh at $3,300 with Mayfield ruled out. Backup-quarterback pressure is the thesis; Steelers secondary injuries and return/turnover variance remain risks.

snapshots.summary: Keep eight selections and replace Allgeier with Likely at the same $4,800 FLEX cost. Prefer documented receiving opportunity while preserving the Rams core; official export now verifies prices and eligibility.
snapshots.counterargument: The replacement adds a second Giants pass catcher and removes the Arizona bring-back from an already concentrated three-Rams build. New York's two starting tackles remain questionable. Johnson's absence could add blocking duties rather than targets for Likely, and Allgeier could outperform if Arizona's rushing/red-zone workload wins out.

revisions.reason: Prefer documented receiving volume at the same price over an early-down replacement whose protection duties and small target share limit the PPR case. The relevant role evidence predates this run; it is newly considered here, not overnight breaking news.

projection_comparison.note: Only the 2.7-point selection effect compares the two sets of picks under the same October 18 model snapshot. The older seed estimate stays 134.2; 0.4 of the displayed 3.1-point change comes from model refresh.

source_qualification_change.description: Official export is now accessible and confirms all selected prices/slots. The seed remains labelled as reported prices with no original full export. No salary correction or silent historical backfill.

picks.rationale: Hold the Stafford–Nacua passing pairing. Current platform eligibility and salaries are unchanged; reduced passing volume in a controlled Rams win remains a risk.
Hold the Rams backfield anchor alongside the passing pairing. It provides a rushing route to production but retains three-player Rams concentration.
Hold the verified $5,700 lead-back opportunity with Hall out. The Jets' team report documents heavy recent participation; the matchup and receiving workload still limit certainty.
Hold the premium Rams receiver. There is no observed new injury designation or eligibility change requiring a replacement.
Hold the Giants receiving anchor. The protection concern remains unresolved; retaining him with Likely accepts shared offensive risk.
Hold the $4,000 receiver with Wilson and Skowronek out. The Steelers identify Bernard as an increasingly trusted option, but Metcalf is cleared; do not assume Bernard inherits every missing target.
Hold the $4,100 tight end to preserve the established salary allocation. The refreshed single-model estimate supports retaining him; it does not establish a certain rebound.
Hold the morning FLEX change to Likely. Theo Johnson remains out and the previously documented receiving case remains intact; protection duties could still suppress routes.
Hold Pittsburgh at $3,300 against a Tampa Bay team with Mayfield ruled out. Secondary injuries and turnover/return variance remain explicit risks.

snapshots.summary: Final selection: retain the morning nine unchanged after fresh official availability, slate and salary checks. $300 remains. These players and original salaries are fixed for scoring; later news becomes an observation.
snapshots.counterargument: The build still relies on three Rams and two Giants. Both Giants starting tackles remain questionable in the observed official report, so extra protection could reduce Likely's receiving routes and hurt both Giants selections. Bernard's opportunity is also a role assumption, not a guaranteed target count.

picks.rationale: Choose Stroud at $5,700 after the official team recap documents 312 yards and three TDs in London. Pair him with Noel at a modest combined cost; last week's efficiency is not a projection.
Pay $6,700 for Hubbard's recent rushing workload: 28 carries for 120 yards in Week 6. Keep touchdown and receiving expectations separate from that one-game role evidence.
Retain Allen's 17-carry, two-catch role while the new official export flags Hall OUT. This is conditional on Hall's actual Week 7 availability; the export is not the Friday injury report.
Keep Puka as the one Rams player in this build, at the newly verified $8,400. Seven Week 6 targets keep opportunity on the board; a rebound is a judgment, not a guaranteed outcome.
Keep one Giants pass catcher for his 15 Week 6 targets. McCarthy's relief performance does not establish a full-game passing baseline; quarterback/protection uncertainty remains.
Use Godwin as a $4,300 WR with eight Week 6 targets. The backup-QB environment limits confidence; this is salary relief with observed involvement.

Replace the $5,300 Likely candidate with $4,800 LaPorta to reduce shared Giants risk. Detroit's last game before its bye produced five catches and 88 yards for LaPorta; those results do not set next week's expectation.

Use Noel's $3,900 FLEX price to pair with Stroud. The team confirms four catches for 107 yards and a TD in London; explosive production on only four receptions makes this the most fragile receiving-volume assumption.
Choose Tennessee's $2,600 DST slot as budget relief against Cleveland, whose Week 6 offense scored 13. This is not a claim of a dominant defense or a predictable turnover total.

snapshots.summary: First complete Week 7 candidate: $49,100, $900 left. New official export verifies all nine selections. Retain Nabers; replace the Likely candidate with LaPorta after reassessing quarterback/game-script uncertainty. Pair Stroud with Noel; projections remain unavailable.
snapshots.counterargument: The Stroud-Noel/Nabers game linkage still concentrates three offensive slots in one game, and Noel's four-catch explosive day may overstate dependable volume. LaPorta can lose targets to Detroit's other weapons; removing Likely could discard a sustained role. Allen's lead-back premise fails if Hall returns.

revisions.reason: At $5,300 versus LaPorta $4,800, retain only Nabers from the unsettled Giants passing game. McCarthy relief production is insufficient to assume both receiving lines repeat. This is risk/budget judgment, not a proven player-specific QB effect.

picks.rationale: Keep Stroud at $5,700 using the prior observed 312-yard, three-TD game as role/context evidence. Dell's planned return adds a receiving option; no numerical upgrade is assigned. Removing Noel ends the direct QB-WR pairing.
Keep Hubbard's $6,700 slot and prior 28-carry, 120-yard workload case. No fresh role change established in this focused pass; receiving and touchdown production remain uncertain.

Replace Braelon Allen with $5,300 Pollard. The freshly inspected Week 6 box score records 19 carries for 76 yards, versus one Spears carry; Pollard had zero catches on one target. Prefer that observed rushing role to an Allen lead-role assumption now threatened by Hall's possible return.
Keep the $8,400 premium receiver allocation. Prior seven-target evidence remains the basis; no fresh role-changing report established in this bounded pass and no rebound point forecast assigned.

Keep Nabers at $6,800 for the prior 15-target case. Monday's official transcript still leaves the quarterback decision open and warns against extrapolating desperation offense across a full game; no McCarthy-specific upgrade is assumed.
Keep Godwin at $4,300 for the prior eight-target involvement and price. The backup-QB concern remains; this hold does not certify an improved passing environment.
Keep LaPorta at $4,800 following Detroit's bye and the previously inspected five-catch, 88-yard game. Retain one Giants receiver rather than adding Likely while the QB decision remains open.

Replace Noel with $4,800 Keenan Allen. The fresh Week 6 box score shows eight catches for 82 yards on 11 targets. Dell's confirmed planned return and Harrison's expanding role weaken Noel's already thin volume premise; exact target losses are unquantified.

Keep Tennessee at $2,600 for budget and opponent context. Prior Cleveland 13-point evidence is historical, not a turnover forecast. Pollard plus DST now share exposure to a favorable Tennessee game script.

snapshots.summary: Two new-evidence revisions: Pollard for Braelon Allen, Keenan Allen for Noel. $49,400 total, $600 left. Keep the same official Oct25 Week7 main slate; seven picks and all retained original salaries unchanged. No freeze or point projections.
snapshots.counterargument: The replacements may surrender Allen's better receiving role if Hall remains out and Noel's explosive upside if Dell is eased in. Pollard caught no passes last week; his carry share can change, and pairing him with Titans DST increases shared game-script exposure. Keenan's 11 targets were one game in a loss, not an established Week7 allocation. Stroud is now unpaired with a Houston receiver.

revisions.reason: Official export Hall marker changed OUT to Q; Jets coach reiterates Hall starts on return. Pollard's fresh 19-carry box-score role is preferable to assuming Allen remains the lead back. Hall is not yet confirmed active.

Texans confirm Dell plans to play Sunday and discuss more Harrison involvement. Allen's freshly inspected 11-target game supports a less speculative receiving-volume choice, without asserting a known Noel snap reduction.
